title: Control Board Fault
shortDescription: Main control board has detected an internal error.
fullDescription: F1 on a GE cooktop signals that the electronic control board failed a self-diagnostic. Power cycling occasionally clears transient errors; persistent F1 requires board replacement.
whenToCallPro: For drop-in cooktops still mounted in counter.
videoSearchQuery: GE cooktop F1 control error fix

faq.a: Unit is disabled so no immediate danger; do not bypass.

title: Cooktop Over-Temperature
fullDescription: F2 indicates the glass-surface temperature sensor reported excessive heat. Typically caused by empty pans left on high heat or boiling dry. Remove cookware and allow to cool.

causes.cause: Empty or dry pan on high heat

fixSteps.title: Cool down
fixSteps.instruction: Remove pan, let glass cool 30 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Test sensor
fixSteps.instruction: If recurring with normal cooking, replace sensor.

faq.a: The sensor protects the glass — normal operation should not damage it.

title: Temperature Sensor Open
shortDescription: Surface temperature sensor circuit is open.
fullDescription: F3 indicates a surface temperature sensor (RTD) is open or disconnected. Each zone has its own sensor under the glass. Identify which zone is affected in diagnostic mode.

fixSteps.title: Access sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove cooktop and reach under-glass sensor.

fixSteps.title: Replace
fixSteps.instruction: Install new sensor with thermal paste.

faq.a: Typically yes — only the affected zone is disabled.

title: Temperature Sensor Shorted
fullDescription: F4 is similar to F3 but indicates a shorted sensor rather than open. Same repair path — identify the zone and replace the sensor.
videoSearchQuery: GE cooktop F4 sensor shorted fix

faq.a: Usually pinched wiring or liquid ingress.

title: Touch Key Stuck
fullDescription: F5 indicates a capacitive key is seen as continuously pressed. Clean the glass surface and dry thoroughly. If persistent, the touch controller needs replacement.

fixSteps.title: Clean surface
fixSteps.instruction: Dry thoroughly and use ceramic cleaner.

videoSearchQuery: GE cooktop F5 stuck key fix

faq.a: Yes — use minimal moisture near the touch area.

title: Cooling Fan Fault (Induction)
shortDescription: Induction module cooling fan not running.
fullDescription: F6 on GE induction cooktops indicates the internal cooling fan has failed or is obstructed. Cooktop disables heating to protect electronics.

fixSteps.title: Clear cabinet
fixSteps.instruction: Remove items beneath cooktop for airflow.

videoSearchQuery: GE cooktop F6 fan error fix

faq.a: Consult manual — typically 1-2 inches ventilated cabinet below.

title: Relay Stuck
shortDescription: Element relay on control board stuck.
fullDescription: F7 indicates a power relay on the control board is welded closed, sending power to an element without command. Safety shutdown engages. Replace control board.
videoSearchQuery: GE cooktop F7 relay stuck fix

faq.a: Potentially yes — keep breaker off until repaired.

title: Communication Fault
fullDescription: F8 indicates the UI and power board are not communicating. Check harness and reseat; replace the failed board if persistent.

title: Line Voltage Out of Range
shortDescription: Voltage at terminal block out of spec.
fullDescription: F9 indicates supply voltage is too high or low. Check outlet and supply circuit. Have an electrician verify if issue persists.

title: Runaway Cooking Mode
fullDescription: F10 (sometimes displayed as ER) is a safety fault indicating heating without a corresponding user command. Turn off breaker and call service immediately.

faq.a: No. Keep breaker off until repaired.

title: Stuck key
fullDescription: Touch key stuck. Standard troubleshooting on GE cooktop usually involves resetting power and checking the implicated component.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect power for 5 minutes, then restore.

fixSteps.title: Inspect
fixSteps.instruction: Visual inspection of the implicated component.

fixSteps.title: Test/replace
fixSteps.instruction: Test sensor with multimeter or replace if reading abnormal.

whenToCallPro: If sensor replacement doesn't resolve, control board may need replacement.

faq.q: Can I still use the oven?
faq.a: Resolve before extended use to prevent further damage.
